chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Aban from Hudhayfah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who borrowed a garment, then took it and pledged it as collateral, and the owners of the item came to their item, he said: 'They take their item.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a borrower pledges a borrowed item to someone else?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of *qabd* (possession) in pledge law, establishing that the original owner of the borrowed garment (*'ariyyah*) can directly reclaim their specific item from the third-party pledgee, rather than being limited to monetary compensation. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic view that the borrower's act of pledging does not transfer full ownership rights, allowing the true owner to exercise their right of reclamation (*ruju'*) against the possessor. It highlights the practical application of property rights in commercial transactions within the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* tradition.
